annotations.text:
Nine artboards, all in the Teenage Engineering / Nothing family.

What carries over from your system: Fibonacci spacing, the 1:1.618 split, Space Grotesk + Space Mono, and the instrument metaphor. What gets cut: the soft dual shadow, the frosted glass, the iridescent wash, and champagne gold.

B and I are the same design in two modes, stacked so you can read them against each other. Everything else is a separate direction.

A · SPEC SHEET
The pin, most literally. Light ground, one orange block cutting the headline, hairline rules, monospace annotation everywhere. Work is a numbered list, not cards.

Strongest for the writing.
Tradeoff: reads as a poster.

B · DOT MATRIX (DARK)
Near-black, dot-matrix plates, one signal red, everything in modules like a device UI. Most memorable of the set.

The tradeoff I flagged: every case-study image you have is light, so on black they read as pasted-on rectangles.

I, directly below, is the same design in light. Read them as a pair.

C · FACEPLATE
Your hardware instinct with the shadow removed. One bordered panel, silkscreen labels, part numbers, the dial drawn flat.

Closest to what you already have.
Tradeoff: bordered boxes go corporate fast if the type stops working.

G · TERMINAL SHEET
The ChainGPT pin worked your way: the name as a dot-matrix readout with the cursor, the page as one bordered sheet on a visible grid, a stats strip under every project, the count readout, arrows in their own cells.

Superseded by H on the headline question.

H · MASTHEAD MIX
G's sheet with C's proportion. The display face carries THE HUMAN DOES NOT_ instead of your name; your name drops to the rail where a masthead goes.

The strongest of the light directions, and the one I would build.

I · DOT MATRIX (LIGHT)
B's exact structure, inverted. The dot matrix stops being a lit display and becomes a printed one, which is the more honest reference anyway: Nothing's own packaging is dot-matrix on white.

Note the work tiles. On light, a case-study screenshot sits on the page natively instead of needing a frame to survive. That is the whole argument for having this mode.

The rail carries a real toggle rather than a sun-and-moon icon.

TOGGLE, OR A ROLE SPLIT?

Two different products, worth deciding before either gets built.

A TOGGLE is a viewer preference: both modes work on every page, every component carries two palettes, and your case-study images have to hold up on both grounds. More work, and the images are the hard part.

A ROLE SPLIT is an editorial decision: the home page is dark because it is pure type and the dial and it is strongest on black; case studies are light because they are full of light screenshots. No toggle, no doubling, and each page gets the ground its content actually wants.

My read: build the role split first. It is most of the effect for a fraction of the work, and it needs no state. Add the toggle later only if someone asks for it.

D · EXPLODED VIEW
Cool grey-blue, the page as a technical assembly drawing of you: three layers on an axis, leader lines to a keyed legend, work as a parts list.

Tradeoff: the diagram has to be genuinely well drawn, and it is the most work to keep updated.

E · TYPE SPECIMEN
1995 and 2026 set enormous at either end with the arc plotted between. Says thirty-one years without a sentence of bragging.

Tradeoff: commits hard. If the numbers stop being the story, the layout has to change.

F · GRAPH PAPER
The quietest. Visible engineering grid, monospace first, everything plotted to coordinates, Fibonacci tick strips.

Closest in spirit to the math your system is built on.
Tradeoff: quiet can read as unfinished.
